bottleneck.evidence: The stock Nsight Compute reports under profile/dsa-prefill-trtllm-m4096-stock-20260722 show long-scoreboard stalls concentrated around sparse-gather and cross-warp synchronization SASS, while the paired Nsight Systems report shows one dominant proprietary TRT-LLM FMHA kernel rather than a launch-count or tail opportunity. These are advisory production-ABI profiler artifacts, not testbench result metrics.

approaches.summary: Built a deterministic one-GPU rank-local replay of SGLang's exact FlashInfer TRT-LLM paged-FP8 DSA prefill call and captured Nsight Systems plus full and source-correlated Nsight Compute reports.
approaches.why: The profile identified synchronization and sparse-gather pressure inside a proprietary vendor kernel, but exposed no source-editable SGLang kernel seam and therefore was diagnostic rather than a replacement.

approaches.summary: Prototyped an exact-shape, fail-closed SGLang dispatch that passes enable_pdl=False only for the profiled production ABI and preserves FlashInfer's stock policy for every mismatch.
approaches.why: The isolated paired serving-native records and matching profiler reports under evidence/glm52_prod_03_dsa_prefill_attention and profile/dsa-prefill-trtllm-m4096-pdl-off-20260722 did not show a stable improvement, so the trial was not promoted.

approaches.summary: Checked the exact-shape trial against scattered-causal, trailing-causal, and multi-sequence diagnostic index distributions while retaining stock fallback outside the exact guard.
approaches.why: Correctness diagnostics could establish that the policy change preserved outputs for fabricated rank-local distributions, but they could not replace live request-distribution evidence or the required multi-rank production acceptance lane.

lesson: When a production-only sparse-attention replay lands almost entirely in a proprietary vendor kernel, first prove that a wrapper-level policy knob changes the generated kernel or its stable latency before expanding the dispatch surface. If it does not, keep the vendor default and preserve a fail-closed path until the real multi-rank workload and request distribution can be validated.

caveats: No evaluate_task.py result.json exists for this production-ABI session; result speedups, repeat, and conservative gate fields are intentionally null, and no synthetic dsa_prefill_attn gate result is claimed.
The frozen testbench task uses flat BF16 tensors and a different FlashMLA kernel, so it is mathematically related but not operationally representative of the profiled paged-FP8 TRT-LLM path.

Only one authorized visible GPU was available and the local model directory was empty, so live GLM-5.2 reachability, the actual request distribution, full-region latency, and the required TP8/DP8/EP8 production acceptance remain external validation blockers.
The named correctness distributions are deterministic diagnostics, not observed production traffic.
The profiled TRT-LLM kernel is a proprietary precompiled binary with SASS visibility but no source-line mapping.
No replacement was promoted; the final production policy remains the stock FlashInfer fallback.
